tagline: America's largest discount retailer by store count, serving value-conscious customers across 48 U.S. states and Mexico.
hero_kpi_rationale: Dollar General is the largest discount retailer in the U.S. by store count. Its growth is directly tied to the expansion of its network of 20,959 locations, a key indicator of its proximity and accessibility strategy for fixed- or low-income customers.

kpis.name: Number of Stores
kpis.explanation: Total number of company-operated retail locations.
kpis.description: The number of stores is a key indicator of Dollar General's market penetration and growth strategy.
kpis.signal: Undisputed leader in the U.S. discount retail sector.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin reflects the efficiency of managing costs for products sold.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin indicates company performance before interest and taxes.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: R&D spending is not significant for a traditional discount retailer.
kpis.signal: Not applicable to the discount retail sector.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures (CAPEX)
kpis.explanation: Spending on tangible and intangible assets for network growth.
kpis.description: CAPEX represents spending on new store openings, renovations, and technology improvements.
kpis.signal: Indicator of investment in future capacity and expansion.

kpis.name: Digital Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from DG Media Network and digital delivery services.
kpis.description: DG Media Network and delivery services contribute to higher margins and improved revenue predictability.
kpis.signal: Growing and more profitable revenue stream.

kpis.name: Headcount (Employees)
kpis.description: Headcount is a key factor in operational capacity and growth strategy.
kpis.signal: Indicator of workforce size and structure.

kpis.name: Number of Stores Opened (2025)
kpis.explanation: Number of new stores opened during fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: Opening 589 new stores in 2025 is a key driver of revenue growth and market share expansion.

kpis.name: Number of Remodeled Stores (2025)
kpis.explanation: Total number of stores renovated during fiscal year 2025 (Project Renovate and Project Elevate).
kpis.description: Remodeling 4,254 stores (2,000 Project Renovate + 2,254 Project Elevate) aims to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.
kpis.signal: Substantial investment in improving existing store locations.

kpis.name: Number of pOpshelf Stores (2025)
kpis.explanation: Number of pOpshelf stores operated at the end of fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: pOpshelf represents a growth opportunity with 180 stores focused on seasonal, home décor, health, and beauty categories.
kpis.signal: Store format diversification with a specialized concept.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company identifies cybersecurity as a major risk, conducting regular audits and assessments to validate the effectiveness of its controls. The Audit Committee actively oversees risks related to data, IT security, and AI.

risks.title: Macroeconomic and Inflation
risks.score_rationale: The company primarily serves fixed- or low-income customers who are particularly sensitive to inflation, unemployment rates, government policies, and tariffs.

risks.title: Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: The tariff environment is dynamic and unpredictable. While tariffs had no material impact in 2025, announced tariffs could significantly affect costs and customer behavior.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive market with numerous players offering similar products and services, including e-commerce.

risks.title: Labor Costs
risks.score_rationale: Increases in minimum wage, labor cost inflation, and high managerial turnover significantly impact operating costs and profitability.

risks.title: Performance of Existing Stores
risks.score_rationale: The company seeks to improve performance at mature stores, including reducing inventory shrinkage and damages, but these initiatives do not guarantee success.

risks.title: Reputation and Compliance
risks.score_rationale: The company's reputation depends on its ability to serve customers responsibly while complying with increasing government regulations.

ai_positioning.summary: The company did not meaningfully mention AI or machine learning in the provided excerpts from its 10-K filing. AI is briefly referenced in the context of cybersecurity and data risk management, but without details on operational or strategic use.
evidence: Brief mention of AI in cybersecurity and data risk management
